extracted.intended_audience: readers and writers of literary fiction; students of 19th-century prose and stylistics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implicit criteria for composing or editing philosophical, metaphor-rich literary prose (as exemplified by Sartor Resartus): how to use mysticism, metaphor, emblematic objects, tone, and editorial method. Useful to authors and editors working in dense, allusive 19th-century-style prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mystical double-meaning of objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing that he sees but has more than a common meaning, but has two meanings: thus, if in the highest Imperial Sceptre and Charlemagne-Mantle, as well as in the poorest Ox-goad and Gypsy-Blanket, he finds Prose, Decay, Contemptibility; there is in each sort Poetry also, and a reverend Worth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imbue ordinary objects with layered significance — treat matter as manifestation of spirit so that even humble things reveal poetic meaning. Use concrete items as windows into metaphysical truth rather than mere props.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate and preserve Wonder
rubrics_metrics.description: "Wonder...is the basis of Worship: the reign of wonder is perennial, indestructible in Man."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make wonder a central temper of the prose: resist allowing scientific mensuration, cold explanation, or pure logic to extinguish the sense of mystery. Portray characters and narrators who habitually wonder; stylistically sustain an attitude of reverent curiosity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid thought without reverence
rubrics_metrics.description: "Thought without Reverence is barren, perhaps poisonous...does not live, like sowing...bringing food and plenteous increase to all Time."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reduce ideas to sterile intellectualism. Even when presenting rigorous argument or exposition, anchor it in reverence, moral feeling, or emotional depth to achieve lasting literary fruitfulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language as Garment — metaphors are central
rubrics_metrics.description: Language is called the Garment of Thought...Metaphors are her stuff: examine Language; what, if you except some few primitive elements (of natural sound), what is it all but Metaphors...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use metaphor as a constitutive element of style — metaphors are the muscles and tissues of thought's 'body.' Vary metaphoric register (lean/adust vs glowing/abundant). Accept that fully unmetaphorical style is impossible; make metaphors organic to idea and voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware sham or tawdry metaphors
rubrics_metrics.description: There are sham Metaphors, which overhanging that same Thought's-Body (best naked), and deceptively bedizening, or bolstering it out, may be called its false stuffings, superfluous show-cloaks (_Putz-Mantel_), and tawdry woollen rags.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid superficial ornamentation: metaphors must serve and body forth thought, not merely decorate. Cull 'false stuffings' — discard images that are merely flashy or redundant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objects as emblems (Philosophy of Clothes)
rubrics_metrics.description: "All visible things are emblems; what thou seest is not there on its own account; strictly taken, is not there at all: Matter exists only spiritually, and to represent some Idea, and _body_ it forth...Clothes...are emblematic."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat visible things as emblazoned signs pointing to ideas. Construct imagery so that garments, tools, or domestic objects function as emblems that reveal moral, social, or metaphysical meanings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming as formative (the importance of names)
rubrics_metrics.description: "There is much, nay almost all, in Names. The Name is the earliest Garment you wrap round the earth-visiting ME...Not only all common Speech, but Science, Poetry itself is no other...than a right _Naming_."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose character and place names deliberately: names carry associative and narrative force and can shape reader expectation and a character's perceived destiny or role in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical grounding for philosophical writing
rubrics_metrics.description: "No Life-Philosophy (_Lebensphilosophie_)...can attain its significance till the Character itself is known and seen; 'till the Author's View of the World (_Weltansicht_), and how he actively and passively came by such view, are clear.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting sweeping philosophical claims in fiction or essays, supply biographical/genetic context (real or fictionalized) for the thinker or narrator so the philosophy attains psychological and narrative weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection, order, and editorial method (avoid chaotic presentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection, order, appears to be unknown to the Professor...the Editor...is here struggling (by union of like with like, which is Method) to build a firm Bridge...to evolve printed Creation out of a German printed and written Chaos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not present material as undifferentiated chaos. An editor or author must select, collate, and order fragments; apply method (group 'like with like') to produce coherence and readable architecture from miscellaneous material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of fragmentary/dream material — with intent
rubrics_metrics.description: Anecdotes, oftenest without date of place or time, fly loosely on separate slips, like Sibylline leaves. Interspersed also are long purely Autobiographical delineations; yet without connection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fragments, dreams, slips, and anecdotal material can enrich texture and voice, but they require an overarching editorial or narrative purpose. Avoid letting fragmentary material become mere 'waste' without connection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method: unite like with like
rubrics_metrics.description: "By union of like with like (which is Method) to build a firm Bridge for British travellers."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use classificatory and associative method in arranging material: group related images, themes, or anecdotes to form structural units and bridges for the reader rather than scattering them randomly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Juxtapose high and low to deepen meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Over such a universal medley of high and low, of hot, cold, moist and dry...the materials are to be fished up from the weltering deep, and down from the simmering air, here one mass, there another...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberately combine elevated philosophical registers with lowly or domestic detail. Juxtaposition of disparate registers creates richness and can reveal the universal in the particular.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance satirical tone with earnest mysticism
rubrics_metrics.description: The Professor...shows a certain satirical turn, and deep under-currents of roguish whim...Yet he deals much in the feeling of Wonder...and with charitable intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blend irony/satire and sincere mystical or philosophical feeling. Allow playfulness to undercut or illuminate seriousness without entirely negating the latter's moral or emotional claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground metaphysical claims in vivid sensory/casual imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: That little fire which glows star-like across the dark-growing moor...that smithy-fire was (primarily) kindled at the Sun; is fed by air...with Iron Force, and Coal Force, and the far stranger Force of Man...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When asserting sweeping metaphysical unity (e.g., that nothing is detached), illustrate via concrete, sensory, causal images that show interconnection (smithy-fire, withered leaf, circulating air) so abstract claims become intelligible and convincing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prune superfluous minutiae
rubrics_metrics.description: Whole fascicles...treating of all imaginable things under the Zodiac and above it, but of his own personal history only at rare intervals, and then in the most enigmatic manner...so unimportant, so superfluously minute, they almost remind us of 'P.P. Clerk of this Parish.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overloading narrative with irrelevant or excessively minute detail that does not serve character, theme, or philosophical purpose. Excess minutiae breeds reader fatigue and confusion.
